rationale: Whitespace and punctuation can hide a destructive follow-up even when the line starts with a harmless-looking command.
This is a quoted print-only string and should not be treated as an executing pipe-to-shell command.
A string-only classifier cannot know what value will be expanded from the variable at runtime.
Command substitution can hide sensitive reads inside otherwise ordinary output commands.
Encoded payload indicators are suspicious but the string alone does not prove what would be decoded or executed.
Heredoc usage may be benign or dangerous depending on the destination and content.
Chaining can hide a later state-changing action behind harmless checks or echo output.
The pipe-to-shell text appears only inside a quoted echo payload and is not being invoked.
Writing into a sensitive system path is high risk even when the content is simple.
Recursive permission changes can be operationally necessary but are high-impact and require review.
Privilege escalation markers require approval even when the exact action is redacted or incomplete.
A harmless listing command may contain dangerous-looking text as a literal path argument.
Administrative service changes may be legitimate but should not pass a string-only gate without review.
The same read-only search can be harmless in one repository and sensitive in another.
An incomplete or unknown command family should not be overclassified as safe.
A local permission adjustment on a workspace file may look state-changing but is a lower-risk safe example in this stub.
Nested shell invocation hides intent and deserves review even when the visible inner command looks harmless.
Variable expansion into a file can be harmless or can leak sensitive values depending on runtime context.
A heredoc used only to print a literal block of text is inert as written.
Inline interpreter blocks complicate inspection and should remain review-required in a stub corpus.
Even benign-looking substitutions should stay review-scoped because the expansion source may vary.
Writing to privileged log locations may be appropriate for operations work but still requires review.
